core_obligations: Identify the two sides (proof lines 867-869): the map F(U) -> Cech H^0(U, F) sends a section to its restrictions to the members of the covering, so its injectivity is exactly the separation part of the sheaf condition and its surjectivity is exactly the gluing part.
Conclude the equivalence (proof line 869): since bijectivity of this map for every covering is precisely the sheaf condition, the two stated conditions are equivalent.
proof_roadmap: Recall that Cech H^0 of a covering is the equalizer defining compatible families of local sections.
The natural map from global sections to that equalizer is injective exactly when sections are separated and surjective exactly when compatible families glue.
Those two properties together are the definition of a sheaf, which gives the asserted equivalence.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises abelian sheaves among abelian presheaves on a site: the presheaf is a sheaf exactly when, for every covering, the natural map F(U) -> Cech H^0(U, F) is bijective (statement lines 850-864). The proof is the observation that Cech H^0 computes compatible families of local sections, so injectivity of the displayed map is the separation property and surjectivity is the gluing property, whose conjunction is the sheaf condition (proof lines 867-869). The content is the identification of the map, which is why the author can keep the proof to one sentence. The claim is H2: a definitional identification, stated rather than computed.
